rationale: The accrual leg is essentially ib minus the archive's already-tested payables-adjusted cash flow, so this is largely a sign-flipped re-run of PayablesAdjustedCashFragility layered on the classic earnings-minus-cash-flow (accrual) anomaly, with only the gate asymmetry as new content.

This is a cosmetic variant of PayablesAdjustedCashFragility — the same numerator with a 3-year moving average on apalch and the distress gate swapped to the one already used in SmoothedInventoryLiquidityTrap — and offers no diagnosis of why the prior version's portfolio alpha was insignificant.

Signs are correct (NEG(invch) − apalch rises with unfunded inventory builds, so a negative slope follows) and the move from a two-sided spread to a monotone composite is a genuine, diagnostically motivated test of whether the earlier −3.1 t-alpha was an extreme-leg artifact, though it remains a close relative of InventoryFundingGapDistressSpread.

The double-MIN genuinely requires joint receivable buildup and payables stretch — components with opposing implications under the standard accrual anomaly, so it is not a repackaged accrual signal — and the sign conventions of recch/apalch are handled correctly, with the main risk being thin coverage from the triple conjunction.

The ratio is internally inconsistent with its hypothesis: since |ib − oancf| already contains depreciation, dp/(|ib−oancf|+dp) is highest precisely when other discretionary accruals offset depreciation (total accruals near zero), so a high value indicates the opposite of "gap driven mainly by depreciation."

The expression is syntactically malformed (an extra closing parenthesis after the first SUMRANK block) and, more substantively, ABS of the *net* sum of signed working-capital items measures the magnitude of net WC accruals — a well-known accrual/earnings-quality measure closely mirroring OpaqueAccrualFragility — not the "reporting complexity" across channels the hypothesis claims, which would require summing absolute values.
